v1_problem: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05), and the disputed-bill population is majority ACTUAL-read bills rather than ESTIMATED-read bills (1785 vs 1240 of 3025, E-02). This pattern supports H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE: a change to billing import validation rules around August is causing bills computed from ACTUAL meter reads to be miscalculated or misvalidated and is driving the dispute surge, while tariff change (E-03), slow ticket response (E-04), and field-read/AMI-delivery failures (both rejected against E-02) are ruled out as the mechanism.
v2_problem: Dispute ticket volume nearly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-05). For the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills (1240 of 3025, E-02), AMI read-event data shows 1184 had a valid, timely read nonetheless rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-11). This is caused by validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) comparing the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling=none (E-12), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register values in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13) — making normal v4.2 readings appear ~10x inflated and triggering unwarranted high-consumption rejection and forced estimate substitution. This confirmed mechanism (H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT, H-BV17-UNIT-SCALE-BUG) accounts for the 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-read dispute subset; it does not explain the larger 1785-of-3025 ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-02), whose cause is still unknown.
